properties.description:
DECISION 5, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the wall-check instrument, which reads the SOURCE from outside; this is reflow2 telling you, from inside detect_defects, what its own answer does not cover.

THE MEASURED FAILURE: circular_dependency walked 182 dependency pairs on reflow2's own graph and found nothing - a large, healthy-looking population. ZERO of those pairs joined two subsystem-level components. So "no circular dependencies" was true of the flattened network and said nothing whatever about the subsystems, while reading exactly like a clean bill of health for them. The two real subsystem cycles were found with a hand-written Python script, not with reflow2.

⭐ THE FIRST DESIGN WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is worth keeping. The approved shape was "name the checks that had nothing to examine". Measuring first showed it would print NOTHING on this graph - no rule has an empty population - and would have missed the motivating case entirely. Anthony was told before it was built rather than after. The failure is not a starved rule; it is that A RULE'S POPULATION CAN BE HEALTHY WHILE THE SUB-POPULATION THE READER CARES ABOUT IS EMPTY.

WHAT SHIPPED, two mechanisms because one was not enough:
  · rule_populations - what each of the 8 rules actually walked, and in what unit. Computed with THE SAME EXPRESSION THE RULE USES, never re-derived, because two implementations of one number can disagree. A rule that walked nothing reports clean for the same reason an empty graph does.
  · coupling_by_level - components and dependency pairs AT each declared Component.level. This is the one that bites, and it generalises to any project that declares a hierarchy: the answer is computed over a flattened graph and the reader assumes it holds at the level they asked about.
  · coverage_note - ONE line naming both, present only when there is something to name, so its presence is the signal. A summary rather than a per-finding annotation, because the detail is already in the two lists and a sentence on every finding would crowd the findings.

ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH it now says: "the subsystem level has 10 component(s) and ZERO dependency pairs between them, so every topology result here - cycles, severability, single points of failure - is SILENT about that level rather than clean about it." That is the sentence that would have saved two days.

A FALSE POSITIVE CAUGHT BY TESTING AGAINST REALITY: a level holding ONE component can never have a pair joining two components at it. That is arithmetic, not a modelling gap, and naming it would be the false positive that teaches a reader to skip the line - which is how a signal dies. Fixed before shipping, pinned by a_level_holding_one_component_is_never_called_blind.

THE TOOL DESCRIPTION MOVED WITH IT. detect_defects told readers that swept.rules and swept.note were the whole story, which went stale the moment these fields existed. Updating it pushed past skill_lint's 1500-char cap at 1728; the trim came from a sentence coverage_note now states better. A mechanism is not finished until the message a reader actually sees points at it.
properties.name: A defect sweep says what it could NOT have found — per-rule populations, and coupling at each declared level
